briefings.title: Emergent: How Six Months of Tinkering Led To A $100M ARR Company
briefings.tldr: Emergent, an AI-native platform that enables non-programmers to build and ship functional software through natural language, scaled to $100M ARR and 8.5 million global users within nine months of launch by leveraging deep multi-agent orchestration and a global-first mindset from Bangalore, India.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**  
Emergent, an AI-native platform that enables non-programmers to build and ship functional software through natural language, scaled to $100M ARR and 8.5 million global users within nine months of launch by leveraging deep multi-agent orchestration and a global-first mindset from Bangalore, India.

---

## The Meteoric Rise of Emergent

* **Rapid Scale:** Within just nine months of launching its current product, Emergent reached over $100 million in annualized run rate (ARR).
  * **User Adoption:** The platform has over 8.5 million users across 190 countries, with more than 10 million apps built to date.
  * **Geographic Breakdown:** While 95% of the team is based in Bangalore, India, the primary revenue is generated from the US and Europe, with India accounting for roughly 10%.
* **Democratizing Software:** Emergent allows non-technical users to build, deploy, host, maintain, and monetize real applications purely through natural language chat.
  * **Target Audience:** The tool specifically solves critical technical bottlenecks for solo entrepreneurs and small businesses without dedicated software engineering teams.

## Technical Foundations and "Living at the Edge"

* **Solving the Benchmark:** Emergent originated from a four-person research lab. To focus the team's engineering efforts, they targeted the Swebench benchmark (the premier test for software engineering agents) and successfully ranked World #1.
* **Multi-Agent Architecture:** Rather than building simple co-pilots, Emergent engineered a multi-agent orchestrated system.
  * **Specialized Agents:** Separate autonomous agents handle specific workflows, such as design and automated testing, coordinated through a large, self-learning memory system.
  * **Data and RL:** The system extracts learnable data from every new app built on the platform to constantly improve the agents via reinforcement learning (RL) and fine-tuning.
* **Custom Infrastructure:** The team had to invent its own container systems, disk snapshotting, and memory snapshotting to preserve state across multiple parallel agents.
* **Aggressive Adaptation:** Because underlying foundation models change rapidly, the team has completely rewritten Emergent’s core architecture three times in nine months. 
  * **Predictive Engineering:** The team actively skips engineering temporary patches for current model limitations. For example, they chose not to build custom JSON parsers, correctly betting that the next wave of foundation models (like Claude 3 Opus) would solve that natively.

## From Dunzo to Emergent: Lessons in Failure and Tinkering

* **The Dunzo Legacy:** Prior to Emergent, Mukund Jha co-founded Dunzo, a massive Indian hyperlocal delivery startup that raised $500M+, deployed 1 million riders, and peaked at 10 million monthly orders. 
  * **Operational Rigor:** Jha ported Dunzo’s "watchtower" concept (monitoring physical deliveries 24/7) to Emergent to monitor, flag, and patch failing AI agent tasks in real time.
  * **The Trap of Dilution:** A key lesson from Dunzo was the importance of focus. Dunzo diluted its success by simultaneously chasing dark stores, direct shipping, and marketplaces, whereas Emergent maintains a tight, vertical focus on software automation.
* **The Power of Tinkering:** After leaving Dunzo in late 2023, Jha spent six months in a state of unstructured "tinkering" with GPT-4 and early LLMs. Building tools purely for curiosity and joy yielded the deep, non-consensus insights needed to start Emergent.
* **Intuition Over Consensus:** Jha advocates for solving highly personal problems. Dunzo started as a simple WhatsApp group to solve his own chores; Emergent started because Jha and his twin brother (and co-founder, Madhav) wanted a way to instantly bring their own endless product ideas to life.

## Strategic Playbook for Global AI Startups

* **The Second-Mover Advantage:** When Emergent launched, there were already established AI website builders in the market. Emergent won by focusing on "finishing" rather than "starting."
  * **Real Code vs. Demoware:** While competitors built simple front-end prototypes, Emergent focused on the complex, ground-up automation of real backends, databases, and live deployments.
* **Growth as a Formula:** The company turned user acquisition into a structured math equation, mapping out the precise conversion funnel from social media impressions and influencer partnerships to active platform users.
* **Thinking Global from Day One:** Jha strongly urges founders, especially those in India, to target a global audience immediately. 
  * **Equal Effort:** It takes the exact same amount of founder energy and struggle to build a highly localized company as it does to build a global powerhouse.
  * **Technological Parity:** Generative AI serves as an equalizer, giving engineers anywhere in the world instant access to the exact same cutting-edge tools.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "If you remove all the software companies from Nasdaq and the S&P, you'll see it's been just a flat line [for 30 years]. And we started thinking: what if we can bring this power to almost everybody in the world?" — **Mukund Jha**

> "We took this very massive view that AI progress is going to be exponential and we will always build in the direction of AI, and that sort of led us to think from a problem perspective—let’s automate all of software engineering versus piece-by-piece." — **Mukund Jha**

> "It’s been a prevalent wisdom that actually starting a harder idea is easier, because you can inspire a lot more people to go after a harder problem." — **Mukund Jha**

> "With AI, a lot of things are changing and it's not a time to sort of attack the floor—it's the time to attack the ceiling and think really big." — **Mukund Jha**

briefings.title: FULL REMARKS: War Secretary Pete Hegseth Delivers Remarks In Normandy, France, To Commemorate D-Day
briefings.tldr: At the 82nd anniversary commemoration of D-Day in Normandy, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth honored the monumental sacrifices of Allied forces while issuing a stark call to modern Western leaders to reject complacency, demand reciprocal contributions from allies, and defend their borders against modern ideological "invasions."
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
At the 82nd anniversary commemoration of D-Day in Normandy, Secretary of War Pete Hegseth honored the monumental sacrifices of Allied forces while issuing a stark call to modern Western leaders to reject complacency, demand reciprocal contributions from allies, and defend their borders against modern ideological "invasions."

---

## Honoring the Legacy and Scale of D-Day
* **The 82nd Anniversary:** Secretary Pete Hegseth commemorated 82 years since the historic landings, calling the Normandy American Cemetery a monument to the unyielding spirit of the American warrior and a testament to the supreme sacrifices made to liberate Europe from Nazi tyranny.
* **Unprecedented Scale and Engineering:** Hegseth highlighted the immense logistics and industrial might that fueled the invasion.
    * **The Armada:** Recalled the words of Sergeant William Ashbrook of the 101st Airborne, who remarked that there were so many ships in the English Channel "that it seemed as if you could step out of the plane and walk to France on top of them."
    * **Higgins Boats:** Praised the blue-collar grit of the 20,000 workers in New Orleans who manufactured the Higgins landing craft, enabling troops to storm Omaha and Utah beaches.
* **Reviving the Warrior Ethos:** Hegseth emphasized that the Department of War is actively working to revive the uncompromising warrior ethos embodied by the Greatest Generation.

## Redefining Alliances: Shared Sacrifice vs. Empty Slogans
* **True Alliances Require Action:** Hegseth stressed that the victory of Operation Overlord was achieved because every partner nation brought its full measure of industry, courage, and blood.
    * **The Critique of Modern Diplomacy:** He argued that effective alliances are built on "real allies doing real things, taking real losses" rather than "empty slogans, lavish summits, or communiques."
* **Reciprocal Defense Burden:** While affirming that America must and will lead, Hegseth stated that Western allies must be capable, ready, and willing to stand shoulder-to-shoulder in the breach.
* **Peace Through Strength:** He warned that some Western capitals have grown too comfortable, forgetting that peace is not merely wished into being, but bought with strength, readiness, and political will.

## Modern Threat Landscapes and the Defense of the West
* **The Modern "Invasion" of Europe:** Hegseth drew a direct parallel between the storming of Normandy's beaches and contemporary migration and ideological challenges facing Europe today.
    * **Vulnerable Borders:** He pointed out that beaches in Spain, Italy, Greece, and Bulgaria are being "stormed by different dangerous ideologies" via arriving boats and men.
    * **A Warning to European Leaders:** Hegseth openly questioned when European capitals will take action to stop this "invasion" before it is too late to maintain the freedom secured in 1944.
* **Defending Western Tradition:** Invoking President Ronald Reagan, Hegseth reminded the audience that freedom is never more than one generation away from extinction and must be unapologetically defended.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "Real allies doing real things, taking real losses for a shared cause worth fighting and dying for. Each nation pulled its weight. Each nation bled. America will lead, and we must. But capable allies must be right there with us, shoulder to shoulder in the breach when it matters."  
> — **Pete Hegseth**

> "Sadly, today, different European beaches are stormed by different dangerous ideologies. Beaches in Spain, in Italy, in Greece, and Bulgaria. Boats and men arrive. When will European capitals do something about that invasion? Or is it too late?"  
> — **Pete Hegseth**

> "Some trust in chariots, and some in horses, but we, but we trust in the name of the Lord our God."  
> — **Pete Hegseth** *(quoting Psalm 20:7)*

briefings.title: The IPO Comeback: Why Tech Giants Are Finally Going Public | All-In Liquidity IPO Panel
briefings.tldr: The tech landscape is undergoing a critical shift as newly public pioneers Cerebras Systems and Planet Labs demonstrate how real-time silicon architecture and space-based data infrastructure are converging to build the next generation of "Large Earth Models."
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The tech landscape is undergoing a critical shift as newly public pioneers Cerebras Systems and Planet Labs demonstrate how real-time silicon architecture and space-based data infrastructure are converging to build the next generation of "Large Earth Models."

---

## The Reality of Going Public and the IPO Pendulum

*   **The Overhead of IPOs:** Andrew Feldman (CEO, Cerebras Systems) noted that the process of going public involves massive administrative friction, including "garbage meetings" of up to 130 attendees and endless document revisions. However, the event serves as a massive cultural milestone and point of pride for long-term employees and their families.
*   **Corporate Legitimization:** Will Marshall (CEO, Planet Labs) emphasized that being a public company provides critical validation, reassuring enterprise and government clients that the business is financially stable and structurally permanent.
    *   **Revenue Mix:** Security and defense contracts now account for roughly 60% of Planet Labs’ business, driven by geopolitical demands for early threat detection.
*   **Post-IPO Value Accrual:** Panelists agreed that the vast majority of historical tech investment returns occur *after* a company goes public, rather than during its private stages. 
    *   **Market Shifting:** While mega-caps like SpaceX and OpenAI have kept their massive valuation jumps in the private markets, Brad Gerstner (CEO, Altimeter Capital) noted that the pendulum is swinging back. More companies are aiming to go public at earlier valuations ($1 billion to $5 billion) to let public markets participate in their hyper-growth phase.
*   **Lock-up Innovations:** Cerebras and their banking partners pioneered a "dribble lock-up" structure, allowing investors to systematically liquidate shares over a six-month window based on specific performance hurdles. SpaceX is reportedly preparing a similar mechanism.

## The Horizon for Space-Based Data Centers

*   **Launch Cost Milestones:** Satellite launch costs have dropped nearly 10x over the last decade to roughly $1,000 per kilogram. Once launch costs reach $200–$300 per kilogram—a milestone expected in 2 to 3 years via SpaceX's Starship—it will be cheaper to run data centers in space than on Earth.
*   **The Space Power Advantage:** Terrestrial data centers face massive energy and battery storage constraints. In space, servers placed in sun-synchronous "dawn-dusk" orbits can view the sun 24/7, capturing five times more solar energy per panel than on Earth without requiring complex battery backups.
*   **Hardware Deployments:** 
    *   Planet Labs has already launched Nvidia GPUs into space and is currently partnering with Google to test Google TPUs in orbit.
    *   Marshall projects that within 10 years, a majority of the world's heavy compute will be deployed in space.
*   **Technical Caveats:** Feldman cautioned that space-based compute faces immense hurdles, particularly regarding the high-speed clustering and inter-chip networking protocols that remain incredibly difficult to optimize even on Earth.

## Redefining AI Silicon Architecture

*   **The AI Data Bottleneck:** The primary limitation in modern computer architecture is not processing speed, but the latency and energy required to move data from memory to the compute core.
*   **Wafer-Scale Innovation:** To solve this bottleneck, Cerebras rejected standard GPU design architecture. Instead of building standard postage-stamp-sized chips, they engineered a dinner-plate-sized "wafer-scale" chip that places massive amounts of memory directly adjacent to the processing cores.
*   **Real-World Speed Advantage:** This specialized design allows Cerebras systems to run OpenAI workloads 15 to 18 times faster than standard Nvidia GPUs. 
*   **The Real-Time Mandate:** Feldman highlighted that just as the market for "slow web search" or "dial-up internet" went to zero, the market for slow AI will also collapse. Real-time inference speeds are non-negotiable for future consumer and enterprise adoption.

## The Convergence of AI and Earth Data

*   **Beyond Text-Based LLMs:** Marshall observed that current Large Language Models are "blind" to physical reality because they are trained almost exclusively on internet text. They lack direct observation of physical events, agricultural trends, and ecological disasters.
*   **Large Earth Models (LEMs):** By combining space-based imaging (Planet Labs captures a complete visual scan of the Earth daily) with space-based AI compute, developers can construct "Large Earth Models" to automate decision-making for agriculture, energy grid management, infrastructure permitting, and global security.

---

## Notable Quotes

> "I think you do all this work and I think it's really difficult to overestimate the amount of garbage that's involved in going public... the next morning you've sold no more stuff, your engineering projects have made no progress since the day you weren't public, and you go back to work."
> — **Andrew Feldman**

> "Our view as computer architects is if you want to be 20 times better than somebody, your architecture can't look like them. They have enjoyed and eaten all the low-hanging fruit. So if you build a GPU, the odds that you're better than Nvidia in our view are approximately zero."
> — **Andrew Feldman**

> "All the cool stuff that we're doing with LLMs now is really based on just the text of the internet being absorbed into these models... But they don't know shit about the real world. If you give them real-world data, then they can answer real-world problems. And that's going to open up gazillions of applications."
> — **Will Marshall**
